about_the_game:
What if You had to fight the DragonBorn, Because he had turned to the dark side.?

Somewhere between a Casual open-world RPG and a wizard/Alchemist wet dream...

I like to play open-world Dnd types games, and I always play magic wielders,,, with alchemy for back-up. So here is my game, build around those things.

As a Fighter: Wield a sword, improve it, and even enhance it with magic. Face off against ten mythological monsters in the first main mission. 

As a Rogue: Master the art of stealth, equip throwing stars or daggers, and sneak into dragon hideouts to deliver a deadly backstab that could even decapitate them—or perhaps just steal some of their precious treasures. This is the second main mission: finding the lost Dragon Orbs that control the dragons.

As a Wizard: Choose your magic school—focus on war, defense, or even the dark art of necromancy. Harness the power within you to fight undead beasts, and in time, you may even gain control over them. This is the final main mission, but its secrets will remain hidden... for now.

Races: There are five races, the classics from 'Lord of the Rings'.

Humans are average, and can be everything. Fighter, Rogue or Wizard.

Dwarfs have good constitution, which makes them able to fighter for a long time.

Elves are tall, and flexible, perfects for range weapons, or magic wielding.

Orc are strong, but stupid, perfect for a fighter.

Half-lings are short, nimble and charming, perfect for Rogues.

Magic in this game is wild...

It has to be because you are fighting against mythical creatures like Minotaurs, Medusa, and the Basilisk, which can paralyze. And deep beneath the dwarf kingdom in the North, there are rumors of something dark waiting to be released.

This game is an open-world, single player RPG game.
You can play it casually, taking your time to do quests and explore the world, or you can play it more hard-core.

I like to play open-world RPGs like Skyrim, Oblivion, and Morrowind, as well as Tolkiens universe. So, I have taken the parts I like from them: the wild magic and alchemy from Morrowind, the bright colors from Oblivion, and Skyrim's weapon improvements.
